description: A deeper form of impetigo in which bacterial infection extends into the skin and produces ulcerated crusted lesions.
causes: Usually bacterial infection, commonly Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes
risk_factors: Poor hygiene or crowded living conditions

appearance.general: Crusted, punched-out ulcers with a thick adherent crust may occur, often on the lower legs.

warning_signs: Spreading redness, increasing pain, fever, or systemic illness requires medical assessment.
prevention: Clean and protect minor skin injuries.
Avoid sharing towels and other personal items when infection is present.
